description: Propose a Panel from candidate ids of an open page. Banquish confirms it on the page, which the first Panel from it takes over as its own. The page stays open to you for more Panels: its ids stay valid for expand, find, add_panel and update_panel, and each further Panel gets a fresh copy of the page, where Banquish replays your reveals and finds the parts again, which takes a few seconds (refused if they aren't found). It answers within about 45 s: a Panel whose page is still loading then gives its id with "loading"; a later Fit report or read_workspace shows it settled. reveal and screenshot need the page opened again once a Panel has taken it. Each id is one part: take the smallest part that answers. Several ids make one Composite Panel, for parts of the page that act on each other (a player and its transcript, a chart and its time picker): they show together in one tile and stay live together. exclude takes ids of candidates inside the chosen parts that the Panel leaves out (the site's buttons and menus, an ad, a reply box, the rest of a container whose text you want); any other id is refused with the reason. Mode is "item" (follow this specific thing, the default) or "spot" (whatever occupies this place). Placement is where its Tile goes on the Workspace's grid, as in arrange; without one it goes full width below the last Tile. A width below a Panel's minimum width is taken, and its Panel shows scaled down to as little as 85% of that minimum on the user's screen; below 85% of it, the whole Workspace shows as one column. With h, a Panel's Tile is that tall: a taller Panel scrolls inside it, and a shorter one shows centred in it, which the Fit report mentions. Returns the Fit report: at the user's window, which Tiles are scaled below their Panel's minimum width, scroll inside, fell back to crop, are broken or ambiguous, or leave their Tile's width unused, and any gaps between Tiles; and, not as an issue, which Panels are shorter than the h of their Tile, so show centred in it. A Tile whose page hasn't laid it out at its width yet (one not on screen, say) is settling: a later report says how it fits. While a settling Tile's minimum width isn't known, whether the Workspace shows as one column isn't either: oneColumn is left out, and the summary says so.
name: add_panel
title: Add a Panel
